content: Rego policies default-deny: start every package with 'default allow := false' and only grant via explicit allow rules. A new endpoint or action that lacks an allow rule must be denied, not silently permitted.

name: Gateway path validator must match the OpenAPI route shape exactly
description: When a gateway Rego policy validates request paths, the validator must mirror the OpenAPI route shape exactly — same number of segments, same fixed vs variable positions. An off-by-one segment count silently rejects valid requests (403) or, worse, matches an unintended route. Add a test per path validator that asserts both a valid and an invalid path.

OPA running with '--watch' on a mounted policy directory does not always reload after the files change — especially after a branch switch that swaps the files underneath the mount. The on-disk content updates but OPA serves the previously-loaded bytes from cache, causing valid requests to 403 because the new allow rule isn't loaded.
resolution: Restart the OPA container after editing or branch-switching policies. Verify what OPA actually loaded with: curl -s $OPA/v1/policies/<id> | jq -r .result.raw | grep <new_rule>. Treat this like any mounted-dir container cache (same class as wiremock/stale-mapping issues): restart on change.

name: Widening-flag test discipline: pin strict explicitly, pin the invariant not the boolean
description: When a policy gains a config-widened branch (ADR 0022 root-read exemption via data.config), existing test cells that pinned the strict behavior break under the new shipped default. The fix is NOT to delete them: re-pin them explicitly ('with data.config as {}') so the strict mode stays covered, and add flag-state cells for the new default + absent-flag + explicit-false. Crucially, re-read WHAT the old cells pinned: the 7.0.5 catalog High's cells (R5/R6) pinned list<->GET AGREEMENT, not one-sided strictness — the exemption preserves the invariant (both pass) while flipping the boolean. Also: keep 'absent config = strict' so a widening only ever activates by explicit deployment choice, and verify the residual shape empirically in BOTH flag states (opa eval --partial; a data-guarded branch folds the tag conjunct clean out of the residual when the flag is concrete-true).

name: Catalog filter rule: role-def-only, NO tag conjunct, governed-scope-composed
description: Slice B4 added a 'filter' entrypoint to catalog.rego that DIFFERS from category.rego's filter: it has NO tag conjunct. Catalogs are not tag-filtered — visibility is a team-membership question resolved app-side (GovernedScopeResolver supplies the 'id IN (governed ids)' base scope). So catalog.filter only decides 'may this role LIST catalogs at all': has_role_definition + inline category-token expansion (data.permission_categories) must contain 'list' + not filter_list_denied. Role-def-only (no subject-roles fallback) so a missing role-def fails closed. Verified empirically via the REAL Compile API (POST /v1/compile, unknowns=[input.resource], query data.catalog.filter==true): role grants list -> queries=[[ eq("catalog", input.resource.type) ]] = a tautology over catalog rows = ALLOW_ALL (composes as governedScope AND true); NO role-def -> queries=null = DENY_ALL (the fail-OPEN trap boundary, mx-a932a0 — null/{} = DENY_ALL); role DENIES list -> queries=[[ eq(type) AND not eq(type) ]] = contradiction = DENY_ALL. The list-denying residual is a negated type-eq (unsupported-negation-survives-PE, mx-cbd39e) -> fails closed to the batch recheck (allow). Also B4: the blanket realm-role fallback was removed from catalog/category/product single-decision paths; the ONLY surviving fallback is verb-gated 'allow if verb==create && not has_role_definition && catalog-editor in roles' (type-level onboarding precedes any team). opa test 183->188; opa check --strict clean.

catalog.rego 'filter' (list residual) omits the filter_tags_satisfied conjunct that catalog.allow (single-GET) AND category.rego's own filter both enforce. For a TAG-GATED catalog role, catalog.filter partial-evaluates to an unconditional ALLOW_ALL (opa eval --partial: empty-body residual = tautology), while category.filter carries the tag predicate (input.resource.attributes.region = "emea") and catalog.allow returns false on a mismatched catalog. Net: GET /catalogs LISTS a tag-mismatched catalog's full DTO that GET /catalogs/{id} correctly 403s — a list-vs-single-GET control divergence. Bounded to the caller's already-governed set (no cross-tenant escape, read-only metadata) => High not Critical. AGGRAVATOR: the triggering role is SELF-AUTHORABLE — RoleDefinitionService.validateContract validates only roleLevel/categories/ceilings and passes required_tags+match_mode through unchecked (create L80-84, update L96-101), so a team admin (ADR 0009 self-service) can deliberately mint {catalog:[READ], required_tags:{region:[emea]}, match_mode:ANY_OF}. Found by the 7.0.5 baseline security review (commit b7ad6a7). Confirmed independently on OPA 1.10.1.
resolution: Report-only in 7.0.5; fix on a follow-up branch off b7ad6a7. Port category.rego's filter_tags_satisfied/filter_key_satisfied (category.rego:236-260) into catalog.rego's filter so the list residual carries the tag predicate; add filter tests for a TAG-GATED catalog role (existing R1-R3 only cover tag-free roles) asserting list<->single-GET agreement on a region-mismatched catalog. Secondary hardening seam: validate required_tags/match_mode in RoleDefinitionService.validateContract. See docs/code-review/PHASE-7-BASELINE-SECURITY-REVIEW.md.

description: Per-type policy sibling-drift fail-open: catalog.rego shipped WITHOUT the 'denied if input.resource.attributes.abac_deny == true' rule + 'not denied' conjunct on allow that category.rego and product.rego both carry. Result: a catalog flagged abac_deny=true is hidden from GET /catalogs (the SQL notDenied mirror in AbacQueryService runs for catalogs) but stays viewable/updatable/DELETABLE via the single-resource @OpaPreAuthorize gates — a list-vs-single-GET fail-open on the ROOT type, violating ADR-0010 §3 (single-GET and list must agree on 'denied'). The SQL side of the mirror was ported to the root type; the Rego side never was. Coverage gap corroborated: catalog_test.rego has ZERO abac_deny cells (category has 5, product 1) — nothing asserted the override on the root type because it did not exist. Bounded to a member already governing the catalog (B4 membership gate is upstream), so High not Critical, but includes DELETE (destructive). Found by the 7.4 pre-publish delta security review (2026-07-12); confirmed via opa eval, OPA 1.10.1.
resolution: FIX DIRECTION (follow-up branch, not applied): port 'denied if abac_deny==true' + 'not denied' onto catalog.rego allow, matching the siblings; add catalog_test.rego abac_deny cells (single-GET view/update/delete all deny; list-vs-single-GET agreement). GENERALIZE: when a security invariant (deny-override, tag conjunct, fail-closed filter) is implemented per-type across N sibling .rego policies, a diff/grep parity sweep across ALL siblings (grep -c the invariant token per policy + per test file) is mandatory — the root type is the one most likely skipped because it was written first. The 7.0.5 baseline already fixed the sibling catalog *filter* tag-drop; this is the single-GET half of the same root-type blind spot.

name: ANY_OF / ALL_OF tag match in Rego (some-in / every) with vacuous back-compat + fail-closed
description: To match a role's required_tags ({key:[acceptable]}) against a resource whose tag value may be a SCALAR or an ARRAY, in OPA 1.x: (1) normalize the resource value to a SET — resource_tag_values(key) with three mutually-exclusive bodies (is_array -> {elements}, not is_array -> {scalar}, absent -> set()); (2) key_satisfied(key,acceptable) = existential intersection 'some v in resource_tag_values(key); v in acceptable'; (3) tags_satisfied for ANY_OF via 'some key,acceptable in required_tags; key_satisfied' (existential) and for ALL_OF via 'every key,acceptable in required_tags { key_satisfied }' (universal). Make the no-requirement case a SEPARATE vacuous body ('not has_required_tags' where has_required_tags := count(required_tags)>0) so untagged roles are unaffected (back-compat). Crucially: do NOT add an explicit error rule for a malformed requirement — let a present-but-unknown match_mode match none of the quantifier rules and not be vacuous, so tags_satisfied simply fails -> deny (fail-closed). 'allow' then requires BOTH the permission AND tags_satisfied. This is the OPA-native expression of attribute-based grants and the on-ramp to Phase-7 ReBAC-in-policy. Prove the decisive contrast with opa eval: same role, two resources differing only in tags -> one allow, one deny.

name: Coarse list-gate rego clause: open the type-level @OpaPreAuthorize gate for an inheritable ancestor grant on a LIST
description: Slice 5.5-B's one design fork the planning didn't pin (settled with the maintainer). The type-level @OpaPreAuthorize(<type>:read) on a LIST endpoint evaluates  with only a resource TYPE (no id, no ancestors), so inherited_grant (which needs ancestors) can't fire -> a subject whose role grants read ONLY on an inheritable ancestor (e.g. {catalog:[read]}) — the very subject the subtreeSpec widening exists for — is denied 403 at the COARSE gate before the SQL widening runs (opa eval confirms allow=false). FIX: a small ADDITIVE second `allow` clause: allow if { not input.resource.id ; not denied ; list_inheritable_grant } where list_inheritable_grant if { some ancestor_type,_ in data.category.inheritable[input.resource.type] ; verb in input.role_definition.permissions[ancestor_type] }. It ONLY opens the coarse 'may you read <type> at all' gate; the FINE which-rows cut still happens in SQL (the app-built subtreeSpec). Scoped to a LIST via  so single-resource decisions are byte-unchanged (a dedicated opa-test pins this); AND-s ; opt-in/default-off via the same data.<pkg>.inheritable 5.5-A ships (NO new data); a stranger with no role_definition can't pass. PLANNING FEEDBACK: a list-WIDENING slice must ALSO open the coarse list gate for inheritable grants, or the e2e 403s before the widening. Proven by run-hierarchy-list-matrix.sh through the gateway (10/10) + 5 new opa tests (77/77).

content: OPA authorization helpers MUST fail closed: any error talking to OPA, any timeout, any unparseable response, or any ambiguity denies the request. Never default to allow on failure. The OPA client should treat a non-200 / connection error as 'deny' and surface it, not swallow it into 'true'.

name: Category-driven team.rego: two-rule allow (effective_actions + owner-only-by-code fence) mirrored byte-for-byte across both bundles
description: Phase 6.7 made the control plane category-driven, symmetric with catalog.rego. team.rego's allow is TWO rules: (1) category-driven — guard on input.role_definition.permissions, then 'verb in permissions.effective_actions(input.role_definition, input.resource.type)' (the SAME shared expansion home the catalog uses; import data.permissions); (2) an owner-only FENCE — 'verb in {"define-roles","transfer-ownership"}' AND 'input.role_definition.code == "owner"'. The fence is keyed on the reserved owner CODE, never role_level — verified by opa eval: a custom level-40 role carrying CONTROL still gets transfer-ownership=false. Mirror obligation: team.rego + team_test.rego + permission_categories.json + permissions.rego must be BYTE-IDENTICAL in both bundles (infra/opa/policies + the user-mgmt service bundle); permissions.rego/the table are copied verbatim into the service bundle ONLY so its isolated opa test resolves data.permissions (runtime co-loads from the shared infra bundle). Test-maintenance gotcha when WIDENING a category (READ gained list-members): EVERY assertion that expands that category rises (8 sites for READ), AND any 'deny everything granted -> set()' test must add the new fine action to its denied_actions or it stops being empty. opa test counts: infra 157->177, service-team 14->30.

name: Partial-eval-friendly 'filter' rego rule: role-def-only (fail-closed), flat-verb, scalar+array consistency via member_2 operand side
description: The Phase-5 list-filtering entrypoint added ALONGSIDE the single-decision 'allow' (additive, allow untouched). Two deliberate differences from 'allow': (1) ROLE-DEFINITION-ONLY — 'filter' starts with has_role_definition and has NO subject-roles fallback (model on team.rego). A list request with no role definition partial-evaluates to {} -> DENY_ALL -> EMPTY list, never the whole table (the fail-OPEN leak guard from mx-ff73f1). Prove with opa test: filter false for no-role-def, AND a contrast test that 'allow' DOES grant the same read via its fallback. (2) PARTIAL-EVAL-FRIENDLY tag match: do NOT reuse the single-decision tags_satisfied (its resource_tag_values scalar-vs-array normalize compiles to is_array + set-comprehension AST that a closed-operator residual parser can't translate -> unsupported/deny). Instead write a filter-specific two-body helper filter_key_satisfied(key,acceptable): body A 'input.resource.attributes[key] == v' (scalar), body B 'v in input.resource.attributes[key]' (array). This compiles to a clean 2-disjunct DNF residual: eq(v, attr) + internal.member_2(v, attr). KEY PARSER RULE: internal.member_2 operand SIDE decides the operator — member_2(resourceRef, {literals}) = 'row's value is one of these' = IN (jsonb_extract_path_text ... IN); member_2(literal, resourceRef) = 'this literal is in the row's value(s)' = CONTAINS (jsonb_exists, the ? op). The ? operator matches a JSONB string scalar (string-equality) AND an array element, so CONTAINS covers both — and the two-body filter means concrete rego eval also matches both. NET: list filtering and a single-GET decide the SAME rows for scalar and array tags (ADR-0005/0006 consistency). A negated membership -> unsupported. Also add a 'bulk := [allow with input as item | some item in input.items]' rule for the batch/allowlist primitive (positional decisions; opa test [true,false] + empty->[]). FLAT-VERB only (category:read) — category expansion (READ/WRITE/TAG/GRANT) is a later additive retrofit (ADR 0007 / Phase 6.5), don't anticipate. App adoption: a CategoryListAuthorizer (example code on the public AbacQueryService) resolves the role on the GOVERNING PARENT (catalog, catalogId) like CategoryAuthorizer, builds a query ctx (resource UNKNOWN), and AND-s a catalogId(+parentId) scope Specification into findAuthorized. GOTCHA: in OPA 1.x 'in' is reserved — don't name a test var 'in'.

name: Rego N-level inheritance clause + deny-overrides: granted-then-narrow, opt-in via data, ancestors-in-input
description: To add ancestor inheritance + deny-overrides to a per-type OPA policy WITHOUT breaking the existing direct/fallback/tag logic: restructure to a single 'allow if { granted; not denied }' where 'granted' is an OR of rule bodies (direct_grant, inherited_grant [+ tags_satisfied for tag-gated types], subject-roles fallback). The inherited_grant reads input.resource.ancestors (root-first, leaf-excluded {type,id} list; the role is resolved ONCE on the governing root so role_definition.permissions is keyed by ANCESTOR type) and is gated OPT-IN by data.<pkg>.inheritable[leaftype][ancestortype] — absent ⇒ no inheritance, so with no inheritable data the policy behaves EXACTLY as the pre-hierarchy direct-only decision. deny-overrides is the final narrowing AND: 'denied if input.resource.attributes.abac_deny == true'. Keep OPA 1.x style (no imports), default deny, and any filter/bulk partial-eval entrypoints UNCHANGED (deny-overrides + inheritance are single-decision concerns). GOTCHA for opa test: bundling the inheritable data as JSON under /policies makes inheritance always-on, so the 'opt-in OFF ⇒ deny' tests must explicitly override 'with data.<pkg>.inheritable as {}'. inheritable ships as data JSON files under the OPA policies dir (loaded with the policies); mirror it in the app config for one source of truth.

name: PE-inline idiom: partial-eval filter rules must consume data tables inline, never via user functions
description: OPA's partial evaluator does NOT inline user functions over an unknown argument: a filter rule written as 'verb in permissions.effective_actions(input.role_definition, input.resource.type)' leaves data.permissions.tokens_for(...) calls and set comprehensions in the residual, which CompileResponseParser rejects (unsupported -> batch fallback for EVERY list). The working idiom: consume the SAME data table through a positive inline membership chain ('some token in perms[input.resource.type]; "list" in data.permission_categories[token]') - the known role + known table fold completely, leaving only the type-eq tautology + tag conditions (the 5.x residual shape). One expansion home (data.permission_categories), two consumption idioms: function for full eval (allow/assignable), inline chain for PE. Negation over an unknown-keyed lookup ('not denied[input.resource.type]') folds ONLY when the map is empty; a denial-carrying role degrades to unsupported -> batch recheck via allow (fail-closed, never widens). Verify residual shapes EMPIRICALLY with 'opa eval --partial' before committing to a formulation.

name: Catalog list-filter must mirror category's tag conjunct (PE-friendly filter_tags_satisfied)
description: The list-residual 'filter' entrypoint of any per-type policy that ALSO has a tag-aware single-GET 'allow' MUST carry the PE-friendly tag conjunct (filter_tags_satisfied + the two-body filter_key_satisfied: scalar-eq OR array-membership), or the residual folds to ALLOW_ALL and list leaks rows the single-GET 403s. catalog.rego originally omitted it on the premise 'catalogs are pure-membership, not tag-filtered' (ADR 0018 §3) — incomplete: a self-authored tag-gated catalog role (ADR 0009) breaks that premise. Fix = port category.rego:236-260 verbatim. Verify with opa eval --partial: tag-gated role -> region predicate in residual; untagged role -> ALLOW_ALL (back-compat). The filter's filter_key_satisfied is DELIBERATELY different from allow's resource_tag_values/key_satisfied: the former is DNF-clean (reduces to SQL eq/? existence), the latter is is_array/set-comprehension (does not reduce). Two forms, same semantics, so list<->single-GET agree. Found+fixed in 7.0.5 baseline security review (branch feature/void3110/catalog-filter-tag-fix): High. Also: RoleDefinitionService.validateContract validates the tag requirement (keys/values non-blank, matchMode in {ANY_OF,ALL_OF}) as defense-in-depth.

name: Custom-role management-incapability is defended by TWO independent fences + a JSON-parity drift guard
description: Phase 6.7 keeps custom roles management-incapable with two fences that don't depend on each other: (1) the PROJECTION — EffectiveRoleService.managementRole calls TeamRoleCapabilities.forCode(code), which returns [READ] for ANY non-system code regardless of what the row stores, so a custom role's stored team tokens can never reach the dogfooded policy; (2) AUTHORING VALIDATION — RoleDefinitionService.validateContract now 422s a custom role carrying CONTROL under any key, or CONTROL/TAG under a 'team' key (TAG-under-team would grant define-tags). READ-under-team stays valid (the harmless list-members loosening). Either fence alone suffices; both is defense-in-depth. Vocabulary ownership: 'which categories are authorable vs control-plane' lives in PermissionCategories (CONTROL_PLANE_CATEGORIES={CONTROL}, AUTHORABLE_CATEGORIES={READ,WRITE,TAG,GRANT}), NOT as a literal in the service. DRIFT GUARD: PermissionCategoriesParityTest pins PermissionCategories.EXPANSION byte-for-byte to permission_categories.json (U9) AND asserts the authorable/control-plane sets partition the full vocabulary with no ceiling holding a control-plane category — so adding a category to the JSON without updating the Java sets breaks the build. When widening the table (T1), the Java EXPANSION + these sets must move in lockstep or U9 goes red.

name: Tool-gate document: compute principal-ceiling ∩ agent-capability IN Rego, never in Java
description: agent_tools.rego (Phase 9) authorizes an AGENT TOOL CALL, a different question from the per-type documents: "may this (principal, actor) invoke THIS TOOL at all?" rather than "may this principal act on THIS RESOURCE?". The shape, reusable for any capability-narrowing gate: (1) principal_actions := permissions.effective_actions(input.role_definition, input.resource.attributes.target_type) - the tool DECLARES the resource type it reads, which is what lets the ceiling come from the SHIPPED role model (the expansion is keyed by resource type; there is no "tool" permission key, so without target_type you get an accidental "*" wildcard or always-deny). (2) agent_actions from input.subject.attributes.agent_capability. (3) effective_actions := principal_actions AND-INTERSECT agent_actions - SET INTERSECTION IS THE WHOLE MODEL: it can only shrink, so a capability naming actions the ceiling lacks grants nothing. Keep it in Rego so it is opa-test-able and cannot drift from a Java pre-filter. FOUR fail-closed details that are easy to get wrong: (a) an every-tag-in-tags quantifier is VACUOUSLY TRUE on an empty array - a count(tags) > 0 guard is required or a tool declaring no risk tags sails past the risk condition; (b) an empty allow-list must DENY, not mean "unrestricted", or a profile trimmed to nothing becomes one that permits everything; (c) put the risk ORDERING in a Rego table (risk_rank), not in Java, so one auditable place decides and an unranked tag on either side denies by having no rank; (d) a declared_action_in_category integrity check (the declared verb must be in data.permission_categories[declared category]) makes an unknown category or a self-inconsistent declaration UNAUTHORIZABLE rather than authorized by whichever rule matches. Write a paired contrast test next to the wider-capability-yields-the-ceiling test (same agent, principal who CAN do it -> allowed), otherwise the load-bearing assertion can pass for an unrelated reason. Client-path gotcha: HttpOpaClient.allow POSTs /v1/data/PATH reading result.DECISIONFIELD and allowAll POSTs /v1/data/PATH/bulk, so the policy path is the PACKAGE (agent_tools), never agent_tools/allow.

SYMPTOM: a Rego branch rule meant as 'is this an agent call?' let ONE input shape escape to the wider branch. 'is_agent_call if { input.subject.attributes.actor }' is a bare truthiness test, and in Rego the ONLY falsy value is false — so actor=false leaves the rule UNDEFINED, 'not is_agent_call' succeeds, and the call is decided by the human branch with the capability conjunct skipped entirely. Proven by opa eval against the real bundle with a zero-capability profile on a high-risk tool: actor=false -> allow=true; actor in {"", 0, null, []} -> allow=false. Every other malformed shape correctly denied; false was the single escape.
resolution: Test the KEY, not the value: '"actor" in object.keys(input.subject.attributes)'. DO NOT reach for a type guard — 'is_string(x); x != ""' looks tighter and is strictly worse here, because it pushes "" and null BACK onto the human branch: it widens two shapes to narrow one. The general rule for any Rego rule that ROUTES between a narrow and a wide branch: presence-test the discriminator, because a bare reference is a truthiness test and boolean false is indistinguishable from absent. Pin it with a case per shape (false, "", 0, null, []) in one 'every' loop so a later 'cleanup' cannot silently re-widen. Reachability is not a defence for a policy document that claims independent enforcement of the PEP — the whole point of the second layer is that it holds when the first is bypassed.

description: Adding a CONJUNCT to an existing Rego rule has two silent traps, both hit in SUPERVISED-SCOPE T3 (ADR 0031: ancestor inheritance confined to provenance=='membership'). (1) THE ANCESTOR-LESS PROBE TRAP: a policy test that probes a leaf WITHOUT the runtime ancestor chain returns false for the WRONG reason and green-lights a live fail-open. Slice A's original U14 was written that way, so 4 adversarial rounds passed while catalog:[READ] actually inherited category:view/product:view whenever ancestors were present — which is ALWAYS at runtime. Re-measured before the fix: category:view+[catalog]=true, product:view+[catalog]=true, type-level category:list=true, category:view with no ancestors=false. Always build inheritance probes with the ancestor chain present. (2) THE VACUITY TRAP ON MIGRATION: after the conjunct lands, every pre-existing NEGATIVE test whose fixture lacks the new marker starts passing because of the missing marker instead of the reason it exists to prove (here: 'an ancestor denial narrows the inherited grant'). Counting only the tests that FAIL undercounts the fixtures whose MEANING changed — T3 measured 5 failures but 9 fixture roles needed the stamp.
resolution: Two mechanical checks, both cheap. VACUITY: universally stamp every pre-existing fixture (before the conjunct, all roles behaved as membership-derived, so stamping restores each test's original meaning) and confirm the suite still passes at the OLD count — if an assertion flips, that test genuinely depended on the absence. Leave any 'direct grant unaffected' test UNSTAMPED so the suite itself proves the conjunct reaches only the inheritance path. ANTI-VACUITY for the NEW denial cases: temporarily neutralise the conjunct (membership_derived := true) and confirm every new negative case FAILS (T3: 274->269/274), then restore. A denial case that still passes with the guard removed is asserting nothing. Also sweep every construction site of the input record — 5 'new RoleDefinition(...)' sites existed; the 2 outside the funnel were safe only because they name their types EXPLICITLY (direct_grant) or feed an inheritance-free policy, which must be verified, not assumed.

name: Provenance-scoped tier deny: the two-clause shape (absent + equals), never the naive negation
description: PRODUCTION-TIER T4 (ADR 0030 §3-4 / ADR 0032). To gate a CHILD read on a tag written on its GOVERNING ROOT, for ONE population only, using deny-overrides: two "denied" clauses per leaf policy, each conjoined with the population marker. (A) THE SHAPE TRAP, measured not argued: a single clause "not input.resource.root_attributes.env == production" is WRONG — an ABSENT root_attributes (enrichment failed) passes a negated comparison, so an outage OPENS the tier. Mutation-measured: replacing the two clauses with that naive form fails 6 tests (the untagged-allows and staging-allows cells catch it). The correct shape is TWO positive clauses: "not input.resource.root_attributes" (unproven -> closed) and "input.resource.root_attributes.env == production" (proven production -> closed). Rego semantics that make the middle state work, verified by opa eval BEFORE writing tests: "not {}" is FALSE (only false and undefined are falsy) and ".env" on an empty object is undefined — so a fetched-but-untagged root fires NEITHER clause and stays open. (B) SCOPE EVERY CLAUSE WITH THE POPULATION CONJUNCT (attributes.provenance == supervised), which is what makes "the other population is structurally unaffected" TRUE rather than merely tested: a membership decision cannot REACH the clauses, even during an enrichment outage. Mutation-measured: dropping that conjunct from both clauses fails 24 tests, 21 of them PRE-EXISTING — that blast radius is the proof the scoping is load-bearing. (C) OPEN CONTENTS BY WIDENING THE ROLE (name the child types directly -> ordinary direct_grant), NEVER by re-opening inheritance: the inheritance-confinement conjunct stays untouched and its tests keep asserting exactly what they asserted. (D) "denied" is consulted by both allow clauses and by bulk but deliberately NOT by filter, so the list tier decision lands at the coarse type-level gate and no root_attributes predicate can reach the SQL residual — assert this POSITIVELY (filter is TRUE on the very input the gate denies) so the two are visibly decided in different places. (E) ONE DELETION-MUTATION GUARD PER CLAUSE SITE (4 sites = 4 mutations, each must fail at least one test; measured 2/301 each here) — a clause replicated across N per-type files needs a guard per FILE, since per-type policies drift. (F) Widening a synthesized role breaks every test asserting its OLD shape: here 2 (a unit test and an IT asserting it over the internal resolve wire) — sweep by grepping the factory, not just the module the decomposition named.

THE SHAPE TRAP HAS A CARDINALITY TWIN (PRODUCTION-TIER layer-3 Medium, measured by opa eval): the two-clause tier deny (mx-df8f2b) compared the root tag with a bare scalar == ('input.resource.root_attributes.env == "production"'). An ARRAY-shaped env ({"env":["production"]}) fails OPEN: the equality is false AND 'not input.resource.root_attributes' is false (map present, non-empty), so NEITHER deny clause fires — supervisor reads production contents. This corpus's own contract says a tag value is 'a scalar string OR a string array' and every other tag comparison goes through the resource_tag_values normalizer; the tier clause was the only one that skipped it. Latent here (the env seed pins SINGLE/ENUM and the validator rejects lists) but the reference policy adopters copy, and MULTI is a first-class cardinality for any key an adopter names.
resolution: Any comparison on a TAG VALUE inside a deny clause must be shape-tolerant: '"production" in root_env_values' backed by a normalizer mirroring resource_tag_values (array -> set of elements, scalar -> {scalar}; absent -> undefined, which belongs to the absent/untagged states, never the equals clause). Add the array-production (deny) AND array-non-production (allow — no over-closing) cells to BOTH per-type test files. Review heuristic: grep every new rego comparison against a tag-valued reference for bare ==; the normalizer's existence in the same file is the tell.

name: Sole-blocker structured deny: split 'denied' into stepup_denied OR denied_other so completeness is a rule-graph property
description: STEP-UP-ELEVATION T2 (ADR 0030 §6 Amendment 1). To emit a STRUCTURED deny reason (an RFC 9470 challenge) only when ONE named deny class is the SOLE blocker, do NOT hand-write the 'every other deny' list inside the reason rule. Restructure: 'denied if { denied_other }' + 'denied if { stepup_denied }', move every pre-existing deny body onto denied_other, and write 'deny_reason := {...} if { stepup_denied; granted; not denied_other }'. Completeness then holds BY CONSTRUCTION - no deny body sits directly on 'denied', so 'not denied_other' provably covers every non-step-up deny - instead of being a property of a list someone must remember to update. Put the rule in the file header: ADD NEW DENY CLAUSES TO denied_other, NEVER TO denied; a clause landing on 'denied' is invisible to the negation and leaks a challenge to a subject the second factor cannot help. Corollary that falls out for free: an outage/unproven-tier deny and an agent deny placed in denied_other automatically answer PLAINLY (no challenge), which is exactly the fingerprinting + no-unfulfillable-prompt stance the ADR wanted, without three separate checks. Verify with a grep enumeration of every deny-shaped rule head per file, ticked against denied_other - that enumeration IS the completeness check.

A DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH conjunct can be added, tested through the public rule, and still be completely unguarded. STEP-UP-ELEVATION T2 put 'not is_agent_call' inside 'elevated' beside a separate agent deny clause. Every test went through 'allow'; deleting the conjunct left the corpus at 367/367 GREEN, because the agent deny already closes every path that reaches allow. The mutation guard - not the test suite - is what exposed it: a clause whose deletion changes nothing is either dead code or untested, and 'it is defence in depth' is not a reason to skip finding out which.
resolution: When a conjunct exists to hold IF ANOTHER CLAUSE IS EVER RELAXED, assert the INTERNAL rule directly (both directions), never only the public entrypoint: 'not pkg.elevated with input as <agent+fresh-claims>' AND 'pkg.elevated with input as <human+fresh-claims>'. Re-run the deletion mutation afterwards and confirm it now fails >=1 test. General rule: run a deletion mutation per NEW clause, and treat a 0-fail result as a finding - either the clause is redundant (delete it) or it is unguarded (add a rule-level test). Do not resolve it by deleting a genuine defence-in-depth conjunct.

description: STEP-UP-ELEVATION layer-3 round 3. The elevated rule used data.step_up.loa[acr] >= 2. Rego comparisons are a TOTAL ORDER ACROSS types — every string sorts above every number — so opa eval '"1" >= 2' returns TRUE. A string-valued loa map (a natural transcription slip from Keycloak's acr.loa.map, itself a JSON string) elevated password-only aal1 logins into the production tier, and every aal2 happy-path test stayed green while only the aal1-must-not-elevate deny silently inverted. The rule's fail-closed comment covered missing/non-numeric AUTH_TIME (arithmetic type-errors to undefined) but NOT the comparison operand, because a comparison never type-errors — it orders. Round 5 found the same class on the max_age/skew window axes in the deny_reason coherence guard. The generalizable trap: arithmetic (+, -) fails closed on a bad type (undefined), but comparison (>=, <=, <, >) fails OPEN (well-defined via cross-type order).
resolution: Bind every data-sourced value that feeds a comparison and guard it with is_number() BEFORE comparing: level := data.x.loa[acr]; is_number(level); level >= threshold. Prefer a data-derived threshold (loa[required_acr]) over a literal so the check and the advertised challenge cannot drift. Test with a string-valued map AND a mixed map (string level beside numeric threshold — the sharpest cross-type case). data.* is runtime-mutable via OPA's data API (leaf PUTs), so malformed shapes are a reachable operational state, not just a config typo. Applies to any per-type sibling — sweep all of them (category.rego + product.rego here).

description: STEP-UP-ELEVATION layer-3, rounds 9 and 11. A guard was added to mute an unsatisfiable step-up challenge, written as `max_age >= 0` with the comment "a negative window is unsatisfiable: elevated can never hold". Two rounds later a lens measured it false: the rule `elevated` compares `now - auth_time <= max_age + SKEW`, so max_age=-1 with skew=30 leaves a LIVE 29-second window and a fresh re-auth genuinely elevates. The guard therefore (a) stated an invariant that was simply untrue, which a later edit could have relied on, and (b) was too strict in the answerable direction — it muted max_age=0, withholding the one challenge that would have let the subject in. The same false premise had been copied into the published library's emitter (`maxAge <= 0` -> plain 403). The trap: the guarded VALUE (max_age) was not the ENFORCED QUANTITY (max_age + skew), and the comment asserted a property of the enforced quantity while the code tested the other one.
resolution: When adding a range/sanity guard, guard the EXPRESSION THE RULE ACTUALLY EVALUATES, not the field that names it. Write the guard by copying the enforced expression (`max_age + skew > 0`), then check the comment against it symbol by symbol. Pin BOTH directions with cells: a dead window (-100/+30 and 300/-400) muted, AND a small-but-live one (-1/+30) still challenging — the second is what catches an over-strict guard, which a one-sided "it denies, so it's safe" test never will. Fail-CLOSED over-strictness is still a defect here: for a remedy-bearing deny (a challenge), muting is withholding the remedy, not being safe.

description: STEP-UP-ELEVATION layer-3, rounds 8/11/13 — the same conjunct, three times. Round 8 added `skew >= 0` to deny_reason's coherence guard AND a deletion-mutation cell for it. Round 11 replaced `max_age >= 0 AND skew >= 0` with the single `max_age + skew > 0` (correctly rejecting the false `max_age >= 0` invariant, since the enforced upper bound is the sum). But `elevated` has TWO freshness conjuncts — `now - auth_time <= max_age + skew` AND `auth_time - now <= skew` — so the sum-only guard is blind to the skew axis: skew=-10 with max_age=300 keeps the sum positive, mints a challenge, and a FRESH re-auth fails `0 <= -10`, looping for |skew| seconds. Round 13 measured it. THE MECHANISM THAT HID IT: round 8's mutation cell for `skew >= 0` used skew=-400 against max_age=300, whose SUM is negative — so after round 11 that cell still passed, muted by the sum guard. The deletion guard silently stopped guarding its own axis while staying green, which is exactly the failure mode mutation testing exists to prevent.
resolution: When REPLACING a multi-conjunct guard with a "simpler" single expression, first enumerate every conjunct of the rule being guarded and prove the replacement discriminates on EACH axis independently — a mutation cell per axis, each failing alone. A mutation cell whose fixture also trips a SIBLING guard is not pinning its own conjunct: pick fixture values that violate ONLY the axis under test (here skew=-10/max_age=300 isolates skew; skew=-400/max_age=300 does not, because the sum also goes negative). After any guard refactor, re-run the deletion mutations for the conjuncts you KEPT, not just the ones you changed — that is what would have caught this at round 11.
